ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (66) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

«Разум» (razum, 'reason') is kept as 'reason' throughout, since the tale turns on it: the theologian loses his reason and concludes there is no higher reason, the blind man loses 'his sight and his reason', and the helmsman is 'a reasonable man'; «самолюбие» (samolyubie, 'self-love') is the cause of discord, and «исповедание» (ispovedanie, 'confession') is the word for a denomination. «Магомет» (Magomet) is given in its established English form 'Muhammad', and «Я пен» (Ya pen), the name for Japan, is reproduced as printed.

Source observation: [23] the paragraph ends with a colon («сам молчал:», sam molchal, 'himself kept silent:') although no speech or list follows and the next paragraph begins a new action; possibly a transcription error for a period; translated as printed.

Source observation: [51] the name given for Japan, «Я пен» (Ya pen), is printed as two words; this may be deliberate (cf. Chinese Jih-pen) or a split in transcription; translated as printed, 'Ya pen'.
